name: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
problem: Linear attention has been adopted mainly for efficiency at the cost of quality, and the claim that it can beat full attention under FAIR comparisons had not been established for short-context, long-context and RL-scaling regimes simultaneously.
mechanism: Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), a linear attention module that EXTENDS Gated DeltaNet with a finer-grained gating mechanism so a limited finite-state RNN memory is used more effectively. The chunkwise algorithm uses a specialised variant of Diagonal-Plus-Low-Rank transition matrices, which cuts computation substantially versus the general DPLR formulation while staying closer to the classical delta rule. Architecture: layerwise HYBRID of KDA and Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA).
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): reduces KV CACHE USAGE by up to 75% and achieves up to 6x DECODING THROUGHPUT at 1M context, while outperforming full MLA with a sizeable margin under an identical training recipe across all evaluated tasks. The 6x is a decode-throughput-at-1M-context figure - the regime this architecture targets - and the 75% is a cache-size reduction, not a bandwidth claim.
notes:

So both major engines carry KDA support - among the newest methods in this batch, one of the best-integrated. open_weights=true: the paper states it releases pre-trained and instruction-tuned checkpoints plus the KDA kernel and vLLM implementations. Distinct from moba (sparse attention) and from deepseek-v2-mla (MLA) even though all three involve Kimi or MLA - the hybrid here is KDA + MLA.

  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (926 chars vs 480) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Introduces Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), a linear attention module that extends Gated DeltaNet with a finer-grained gating mechanism so the model makes better use of a limited finite-state RNN memory, plus a bespoke chunkwise algorithm built on a specialised Diagonal-Plus-Low-Rank (DPLR) transition matrix that substantially reduces computation versus the general DPLR formulation. The shipped model, Kimi Linear 48B-A3B, is an MoE hybrid: 3B parameters active per token out of 48B total (about 6.25 percent active), with a gated-delta linear-attention pattern rather than Mamba's scalar-selective SSM. The attention pattern is hybrid: a majority of layers use KDA and a minority use full attention, which is the specific design choice worth carrying into serving work because the full-attention layers are what bound the KV cache. Constant-size state within the linear layers means those layers add no length-dependent memory.

The report gives cache-size and decode-throughput comparisons rather than a single speedup ratio; hardware is reported as H200/H800-class. Treat the 'outperforms full attention' claim as the authors' own fair-comparison framing rather than an independently reproduced result.
